title: Projective modules lift across a nilpotent quotient
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal with $I^N=0$ for some $N\geq1$. For every projective $A/I$-module $\overline P$ [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], there exist a projective $A$-module $P$ and an isomorphism $P/IP\cong\overline P$ of $A/I$-modules. No finite generation is assumed.

proof.text: Put $F=A^{(\overline P)}$, $K=IF$, $Q=F/K$. The canonical linear-combination map $r:F\to\overline P$ is surjective and kills $K$, because scalars in $I$ act as zero on $\overline P$. It descends to a surjection $s:Q\to\overline P$ of $A/I$-modules. By projectivity [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], choose an $A/I$-linear section $i$ and let $\overline p=i s$ be the corresponding idempotent, viewed as an $A$-linear endomorphism of $Q$.

Every $A$-linear endomorphism of $F$ preserves $IF$, so quotienting defines a ring homomorphism $\rho:\operatorname{End}_A(F)\to\operatorname{End}_A(Q)$. Projectivity of the free module $F$ lifts $\overline p\circ q$ through the surjection $q:F\to Q$. Thus $\overline p$ belongs to the image of $\rho$.

For $f\in\ker(\rho)$, its image is contained in $IF$. Linearity and induction give $\operatorname{Im}(f^n)\subseteq I^nF$: map the inductive containment through $f$, commute submodule mapping with ideal scalar multiplication, and use $\operatorname{Im}(f)\subseteq IF$. Since $I^N=0$, this proves $f^N=0$. The two private helpers reductionEnd and reductionEnd_ker_nilpotent implement these constructions and this induction.

Apply the noncommutative Mathlib idempotent-lifting theorem [lem-weil-pbc-noncommutative-idempotent-lift-nil-kernel] to $\rho$ and $\overline p$. It gives $e^2=e$ on $F$ with $\rho(e)=\overline p$, equivalently $q(e(y))=i(r(y))$ for every $y\in F$.

Let $P=\operatorname{Im}(e)$ and $t:F\to P$ be the range restriction of $e$. For $x\in P$, idempotence gives $e(x)=x$, so $t$ splits the inclusion of $P$ into $F$. Thus $P$ is projective by [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

Restrict $r$ to $f:P\to\overline P$. To lift $x\in\overline P$, choose $y\in F$ with $q(y)=i(x)$; then $f(t(y))=x$ by $s i=1$ and $q e=i r$. If $f(x)=0$, then $q(x)=q(e(x))=i(r(x))=0$, hence $x\in IF$. Applying $t$ and its $A$-linearity shows $x=t(x)\in IP$. Conversely $I$ annihilates $\overline P$, so $IP\subseteq\ker(f)$. Therefore $\ker(f)=IP$. The quotient lift of $f$ is bijective by the kernel and surjectivity computations. It is $A/I$-linear by representing each quotient scalar by an element of $A$, and LinearEquiv.ofBijective gives the required equivalence.
